# Dynamic Structural Equation Models

DSEM, multilevel dynamic factor models [@asparouhovDynamicStructuralEquation2018].

## Response decomposition


$$
\boldsymbol{y}_{it} = \boldsymbol{y}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{y}_{2,i} + \boldsymbol{y}_{3,t}, ~ i=1,\dots,N, ~ t = 1, \dots, T
$$

## Within-level model


$$
\begin{aligned}
        \boldsymbol{y}_{1,it}    & = \boldsymbol{\nu}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_{1,it}(L) \boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{R}_{it}(L) \boldsymbol{y}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{K}_{1,it} \boldsymbol{X}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{1,it} \\
        \boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,it} & = \boldsymbol{\alpha}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{B}_{1,it}(L) \boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{Q}_{it}(L) \boldsymbol{y}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{1,it} \boldsymbol{X}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{\xi}_{1,it},
    \end{aligned}
$$

. . .

where

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_{1,it}(L) = \sum_{l=0}^{L} \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_{1,lit} L^{l}, \quad \boldsymbol{R}_{it}(L) = \sum_{l=0}^{L} \boldsymbol{R}_{lit} L^{l}, \\
&\quad  \boldsymbol{B}_{1,it}(L) = \sum_{l=0}^{L} \boldsymbol{B}_{1,lit} L^{l}, \quad \boldsymbol{Q}_{it}(L) = \sum_{l=0}^{L} \boldsymbol{Q}_{lit} L^{l}
\end{aligned}
$$

## Between-participants model


$$
\begin{aligned}
        \boldsymbol{y}_{2,i}    & = \boldsymbol{\nu}_{2} + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_{2} \boldsymbol{\eta}_{2,i} + \boldsymbol{K}_{2}\boldsymbol{X}_{2,i} + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{2,i} \\
        \boldsymbol{\eta}_{2,i} & = \boldsymbol{\alpha}_{2} + \boldsymbol{B}_{2} \boldsymbol{\eta}_{2,i} + \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{2} \boldsymbol{X}_{2,i} + \boldsymbol{\xi}_{2,i},
    \end{aligned}
$$

## Between-timepoints model


$$
\begin{aligned}
        \boldsymbol{y}_{3,t}    & = \boldsymbol{\nu}_{3} + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_{3} \boldsymbol{\eta}_{3,t} + \boldsymbol{K}_{3} \boldsymbol{X}_{3,t} + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{3,t} \\
        \boldsymbol{\eta}_{3,t} & = \boldsymbol{\alpha}_{3} + \boldsymbol{B}_{3}\boldsymbol{\eta}_{3,t} + \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{3}\boldsymbol{X}_{3,t} + \boldsymbol{\xi}_{3,t}.
    \end{aligned}
$$

# Estimation of DSEMs

## Original algorithm (Mplus)

- Sample population-level parameters: $\mathcal{O}(1)$
- Sample individual-specific parameters: $\mathcal{O}(N)$
- Sample timepoint-specific parameters: $\mathcal{O}(T)$
- Sample within-level latent traits: $\mathcal{O}(N \times T)$

Stan implementations [@holtmannModelingWithinlevelLatent2025] have used the same set-up.

# Can we scale it better?

## Theorem


$$
\begin{aligned}
        \boldsymbol{y}_{1,it}    & = \boldsymbol{\nu}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_{1,it}(L) \boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{R}_{it}(L) \boldsymbol{y}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{K}_{1,it} \boldsymbol{X}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{1,it} \\
        \boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,it} & = \boldsymbol{\alpha}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{B}_{1,it}(L) \boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{Q}_{it}(L) \boldsymbol{y}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{1,it} \boldsymbol{X}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{\xi}_{1,it},
    \end{aligned}
$$

. . .

can be written as a linear Gaussian state-space model

$$
\begin{aligned}
        \boldsymbol{y}_{1,it}               & = \boldsymbol{Z}_{it} \tilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{d}_{it} + \boldsymbol{v}_{it}, \quad \boldsymbol{v}_{it} \sim \mathcal{N}\left(\boldsymbol{0}, \boldsymbol{H}_{it}\right)                      \\
        \tilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}_{1,i,t+1} & = \boldsymbol{T}_{it} \tilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{c}_{it} + \boldsymbol{w}_{it}, \quad \boldsymbol{w}_{it} \sim \mathcal{N}\left(\boldsymbol{0}, \boldsymbol{W}_{it}\right),  \\
        \tilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}_{1,i1}    & = \boldsymbol{\xi}_{i}, \quad \boldsymbol{\xi}_{i} \sim \mathcal{N}\left(\boldsymbol{a}_{i1}, \boldsymbol{P}_{i1}\right),
    \end{aligned}
$$

after some pretty tedious algebra.

## Marginalization

Having the within-level model on state-space form lets us:

- Integrate out the within-level latent variables with a Kalman filter.
- Use a sampler which targets the marginal posterior.
- From $\mathcal{O}(N \times T)$ down to $\mathcal{O}(N + T)$.

# Experiments

## Multilevel Scalar Latent AR(1)

$$
\begin{aligned}
        y_{1,it}    & = \eta_{2,i} + \eta_{1,it} + \epsilon_{1,it}, \quad \epsilon_{1,it} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_{2,i}^{2})   \\
        \eta_{1,it} & = \phi_{2,i} \eta_{1,i,t-1} + \xi_{1,it}, \quad \xi_{1,it} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\psi_{2,i}^{2}),
    \end{aligned}
$$

Intercept $\eta_{2,i}$, autoregression $\phi_{2,i}$, and variances $\sigma_{2,i}^{2}$ and $\phi_{2,i}^{2}$ varying between participants.

## Multilevel Scalar Latent AR(1)

![](eg1-univariate-latent-ar1-bulk-efficiency.png)

## Multilevel Trivariate VAR(1)

$$
\begin{aligned}
    \boldsymbol{y}_{1,it}    & = \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_{2}  \boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,it} + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{1,it} , \quad \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{1,it} \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{2,i}) \\
    \boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,it} & = \boldsymbol{\Phi}_{2,i} \boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,i,t-1} + \boldsymbol{\xi}_{1,it}, \quad \boldsymbol{\xi}_{1,it} \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{0}, \boldsymbol{\Psi}_{2,i}),
\end{aligned}
$$

- Intercept, autoregression matrix, and variances allowed to vary between participants.
- 3-dimensional latent state $\boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,it}$. 

## Multilevel Scalar Latent AR(1)

![](eg3-trivariate-efficiency.png)


## Multilevel Latent AR(p)

$$
\begin{aligned}
     & y_{1,it} = \eta_{1,it} + \epsilon_{1,it}, \quad \epsilon_{1,it} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_{2,i}^{2})                     \\
     & \eta_{1,it} = \sum_{l=1}^{p}\phi_{2,li} \eta_{1,i,t-l} + \xi_{1,it}, \quad \xi_{1,it} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\psi_{2,i}^{2}),
\end{aligned}
$$

## Multilevel Latent AR(p)

![](eg4-latent-arp-efficiency.png)

## Cross-Classified VAR(1)

$$
\begin{aligned}
        \boldsymbol{y}_{1,it}    & =
        \begin{bmatrix}
            \lambda_{1,it} & 0 \\
            \lambda_{2,it} & 0 \\
            \lambda_{3,it} & 0 \\
            0              & 1
        \end{bmatrix}
        \boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,it}
        + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{1,it} , \quad \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{1,it} \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{1,i})                                              \\
        \boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,it} & = \boldsymbol{\Phi}_{1,i} \boldsymbol{\eta}_{1,i,t-1} + \boldsymbol{\xi}_{1,it}, \quad \boldsymbol{\xi}_{1,it} \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{0}, \boldsymbol{\Psi}_{1,i}),
    \end{aligned}
$$

Loadings vary both between timepoints and between individuals. Model from @mcneishMeasurementIntensiveLongitudinal2021.

# Beyond Conditionally Gaussian

## Hybrid NUTS-Gibbs Sampler

For categorical responses we can use a similar state-space formulation and do:

1. **Gibbs**: sample within-level latent trait using FFBS.
2. **Data augmentation**: sample latent responses from the normal distribution with a probit link [@albertBayesianAnalysisBinary1993] or the Pólya-Gamma distribution with a logit link [@polsonBayesianInferenceLogistic2013].
3. **NUTS**: run one step of NUTS targeting the marginal posterior.

## Hybrid NUTS-Gibbs Sampler

- Stan does not support HMC-within-Gibbs. Using NumPyro instead.
- Works well for binary responses.
- Fails completely for ordinal responses, due to a well-known issue [@cowlesAcceleratingMonteCarlo1996].

# Going Further

Ordinal responses is the main use case of DSEM and the only published algorithm is @asparouhovDynamicStructuralEquation2018 which scales $\mathcal{O}(N \times T)$.

## Ordinal Data DSEM

Better computational scaling likely requires compromise:

- Laplace approximations which don't cause autodiff to explode?? [@margossianGeneralAdjointdifferentiatedLaplace2023]
- Approximate filtering, possibly with importance sampling correction [@viholaImportanceSamplingType2020].
- Amortized inference [@habermannAmortizedBayesianMultilevel2025].
